name: Joseph-Emmanuel de La Trémoille
summary:
Joseph-Emmanuel de La Trémoille (1659-06-28, France) was a French Cardinal.

De La Trémoille played a pivotal role in the Catholic Church during the Early Modern era. As a cardinal, he participated in several high-level diplomatic missions to European monarchies and contributed significantly to the Church's efforts to maintain its influence in Western Europe.

One of his most notable achievements was his involvement in the development of the Code of Canon Law, which would go on to shape Catholic doctrine for centuries to come. Additionally, de La Trémoille collaborated with other prominent clergy and theologians to promote the spread of Catholicism through education and missionary work.

Despite facing challenges from Protestant reformers and secularizing trends in 18th-century Europe, de La Trémoille remained a respected figure within the Church.

The legacy of Joseph-Emmanuel de La Trémoille can be seen in the enduring influence of Catholicism on European society and politics, as well as his contributions to the development of canon law.

"A true servant of the Lord," de La Trémoille was remembered by contemporaries for his piety and unwavering commitment to the Church's mission.
